title: Saying “that’s so obvious” when someone points out deeper meanings in a film, kinda makes you an anti-intellectual asshole

commenti.body:
That's fair. I think usually when I say "that's so obvious" it's because I'm like the crazy guy at the end of Invasion of the Body Snatchers, shaking people and saying "Isn't it obvious what this person is saying? How could you support this? Don't you see what the implications are?"

And yeah, that's generally unwelcome and unhealthy behavior. But damn, I feel like this is a moment in human history where it's good to think about the underlining ideology in art and try to be more discriminating about which films and filmmakers we support. People will say "How could you support Roman Polanski?" and then go support a fascist movie. Sometimes that makes my blood boil a little.

Sometimes someone mistakes something explicit for being implicit. They get excited they figured something out which is meant to be overt and obvious to begin with. Which idk I agree with you I shouldn't shoot that down. But I guess it's alienating that they're engaging with it on such a different level or something idk. Food for thought for me.

Do you have an example? I’ve never been insulted with such a crass reply. Is someone being rude to you? I enjoyed the symbolism at the end of All That Jazz. The topless women represent the topless dancers from Bob’s youth who inspired his form of dance. I can’t imagine another cinephile jazz dancer rebuking me for noticing that. Only a rude person would say, “No shit, Sherlock.” It may be common knowledge, but it’s still worthy of conversation. Another Fosse film, Sweet Charity. Sure it’s common knowledge that the women are taxi dancers, but how Bob gives them humanity and respects them in the film creates a wonderful post film conversation on the importance of not shaming sex workers. 

“That’s so obvious,” really only works in comic book films. It’s obvious the hero always wins. The plot will crescendo, climax, then a briefer diminuendo. But what are your examples of “that’s so obvious” films?

Honestly, this comes down every time to the way we communicate. Some people are just plain rude and snobby and might very well speak this way in person, but I would venture to say that most would curb their tone and delivery just because it’s never out of style to be a decent human being. 
Online, we have all seen the ways people just love to let their opinions rip without regard for the delivery. It’s old and exhausting. Just be kind. Be better. State your position without condescending tones and engage in good faith. 
I’m not sure why this is so hard for people. I can only guess we all have tendencies to stay within our social bubbles and maybe no one has been loving enough to tell us to stop being an asshole. 😄 
Drop the egos and let’s have some engaging conversation. I’m with you OP
